messages:
sasha: Heads-up: after kernel bump yesterday we're seeing a ~9% drop in prefix cache hit rate on prod for chat completions.

aaron: Yup saw that. Profiling points to mismatched cache keys for requests with system prompt > 800 chars — chunking logic changed how we serialize it.

jin: Do we have a minimal repro? sample keys/logs?

sasha: Posting snippet from a trace:
```json
{"system_prompt":"Welcome to Redwood! This is a long system prompt...","tool_call":{"name":"search","args":"{\"q\":\"hi\"}"},"tokenizer_v":"v2"}
```

kate: Ah — the kernel rewrite introduced a system-prompt chunker that inserts \n markers; serialization now keeps chunks as array for >512 chars. Cache keyer assumes string. So same logical prompt -> different keys.

aaron: We should revert chunker representation in keyer or canonicalize to single string before hashing.

jin: Also saw a bunch of tool args with different whitespace/ordering: {"q":"a","n":1} vs {"n":1,"q":"a"}. Toolcall field ordering kills hits.

deploy-bot: kernel v2.14 rolled to prod at 2026-03-16T02:01Z

kate: :point_up: timeline confirms. Kernel v2.14 changed chunk representation.

sasha: Quick proposal: key normalization flow -> 1) flatten system prompt (join chunks with single \n), 2) canonicalize JSON for tool args (sorted keys, remove insignificant whitespace), 3) include tokenizer version tag, 4) hash with sha256 hex.

aaron: Agree. Also add a backfill job to warmup popular prefixes over last 24h; current prefetch misses after autoscale events.

jin: Perf note: adding canonicalization adds ~0.5ms CPU per request. But cache hit delta should pay off.

kate: Alternative: do lightweight keyer in hot path (string join + stable JSON sort) and heavy canonicalizer asynchronously for cold keys.

sasha: I'll put up a PR with keyer changes + unit tests. Can someone add a perf bench? -> @aaron @jin

aaron: :thumbsup: I'll run bench on staging and compare hit rate simulation.

jin: Will also add a small tool to scan S3 prefix logs for key variance and produce top-100 mismatches.

sasha: Thanks. For rollouts let's do canary 10% and monitor hit-rate and tail latency.
